reconstructed_captions.36: A hand uses a wooden tool to begin burnishing the edge of the leather.
reconstructed_captions.37: The tool is rubbed back and forth, compressing the leather fibers.
reconstructed_captions.38: A close-up shows the edge becoming smoother and more compact.
reconstructed_captions.39: The hand uses fine-grit sandpaper to sand the burnished edge.
reconstructed_captions.40: This sanding step creates a perfectly smooth surface for the next coat.
reconstructed_captions.41: A cloth wipes away the fine dust left from sanding the edge.
reconstructed_captions.42: A brush applies a second, even layer of the edge finishing liquid.
reconstructed_captions.43: The wooden burnishing tool is used once more on the wet second coat.
reconstructed_captions.44: The edge now has a noticeable gloss and a hard, durable finish.
reconstructed_captions.45: The hand holds up the leather piece to inspect the quality of the burnished edge.
reconstructed_captions.46: A piece of heavy canvas cloth is picked up for the final polishing.
reconstructed_captions.47: The canvas is pressed firmly against the edge of the leather.
reconstructed_captions.48: The hand begins to rub the canvas rapidly along the length of the edge.
reconstructed_captions.49: A close-up shows the high-gloss shine developing from the friction.
reconstructed_captions.50: The hand turns the piece to polish another side with the canvas.
reconstructed_captions.51: The entire perimeter of the leather piece is polished to a consistent shine.
reconstructed_captions.52: A finger gently touches the finished edge, demonstrating its smoothness.
reconstructed_captions.53: The fully assembled and edge-finished piece is held up for display.
